# statgpu 0.3.0

## Highlights

statgpu 0.3.0 is being prepared from the merged changes since 0.2.5. It expands
backend-native statistical inference, makes solver and inference choices more
explicit, and fixes important cross-validation, resampling, and reporting
errors. Earlier development entries targeting 0.2.6 are included here; they do
not represent a separate published release.

- **Gaussian inference on the fitted backend.** LinearRegression, Ridge and
  related Gaussian models perform supported covariance, standard-error,
  statistic, p-value and confidence-interval calculations with NumPy, CuPy or
  Torch according to the executed fit. Weighted, rank-deficient, multi-target
  and RidgeCV final-refit workflows retain their documented statistical
  meaning. Final reporting arrays may still be converted to NumPy.
- **Clearer sparse-model inference.** The hardware-neutral
  `inference_method="post_selection_ols"` names the active-set OLS/WLS refit;
  `device` chooses hardware. The penalized coefficients remain the prediction
  coefficients. Public `nodewise_alpha` controls nuisance precision estimation
  for supported debiased sparse-Gaussian methods. Supported smooth
  non-Gaussian L2/no-penalty inference now reports its fixed-penalty
  M-estimation target and requested/resolved method explicitly.
- **Backend-native Gaussian residual bootstrap.** Supported unweighted
  Gaussian L1/ElasticNet/SCAD/MCP residual-bootstrap inference follows the
  fit-recorded NumPy, CuPy or Torch backend and concrete device. Child fits
  preserve the penalty and tuning configuration, with a reproducible residual
  index schedule for a fixed seed. CV inference runs only after selection and
  the full-data final refit.
- **Solver controls with visible execution.** Penalized models use `solver`
  for direct fitting, while LassoCV exposes `cv_solver` for the selection
  stage. LogisticRegression and LogisticRegressionCV add explicit IRLS or
  L-BFGS selection; `auto` preserves IRLS, the weighted summed-loss inverse-C
  L2 objective is unchanged, and `solver_` reports the executed algorithm.
  Supported explicit Newton/L-BFGS GLM fits consistently use analytic weights,
  including domain-aware inverse-link Gamma fitting and CV.
- **More reliable Quantile workflows.** Direct fitting, CV and low-level
  routines reject incompatible solvers or penalties rather than silently
  solving a different problem. Non-median quantiles, unpenalized intercepts,
  sparse accelerator CV and scalar SCAD/MCP objectives are handled
  consistently. Standalone QuantileRegression residual-bootstrap refits use
  the requested quantile and correctly centered residuals; invalid bandwidths
  and unsupported nonuniform-weight inference raise before publishing results.
- **Corrections to everyday results.** RidgeCV uses exactly the requested
  training and validation subsets, including weighted, gapped, reversed-index
  and small explicit folds. Cluster bootstrap samples whole groups instead of
  truncating the last group. LinearRegression scoring handles a single-column
  response without accidental residual broadcasting. CPU SCAD/MCP oracle
  refits preserve family settings, remove regularization, and reject invalid
  convergence or uncertainty rather than publishing plausible-looking tables.
- **Device handling and learning material.** Torch multiple-testing functions
  preserve the p-value tensor's concrete device. Covariance estimators handle
  explicit devices, pandas inputs and supported Torch low-precision inputs
  more consistently; ANOVA rejects nonfinite observations. Torch model-X
  construction uses its input device and local seed. Bilingual tutorials now
  provide explained examples, complete API references and explicit remaining
  limitations.

## Installation and platform support

Once 0.3.0 is published, install the version explicitly:

```bash
pip install statgpu==0.3.0
```

This command targets the future published package; preparing this release
branch does not make the version available on PyPI. The release workflow
builds a pure-Python `py3-none-any` wheel and a source distribution. Package
metadata requires Python 3.9 or newer; the maintained regression matrix covers
Python 3.9–3.12. The CPU wheel is intended for Ubuntu/Linux, Windows and macOS,
with fresh-install smoke checks on those three operating systems. Support for
a CPU wheel on macOS does not establish Apple MPS acceleration.

NumPy, SciPy and joblib are the core dependencies. Formula/dataframe workflows
use the optional `formula` extra. NVIDIA acceleration needs a compatible local
CUDA setup: select either `statgpu[gpu11]` or `statgpu[gpu12]` for the matching
CuPy CUDA major version, or install a CUDA-enabled PyTorch build and the
`torch` extra. Do not install both CuPy CUDA-major extras together.

On estimators using the shared device interface, `device="cpu"` selects NumPy,
`device="cuda"` requests CuPy CUDA, and `device="torch"` requests Torch CUDA.
Explicit unavailable CUDA requests raise; `auto` follows the global device
policy and available backends. Function-level `backend="torch"` can have
separate CPU behavior. Some smoothing, spline and kernel estimators retain
placement exceptions, so consult the
[device guide](https://github.com/TheHiddenObserver/statgpu/blob/master/docs/en/guides/device-and-memory.md)
and inspect actual output devices when placement matters.

## Validation

The following results are historical evidence for the merged implementation
baseline, not certification of the final 0.3.0 release candidate.

[PR #249](https://github.com/TheHiddenObserver/statgpu/pull/249) testing on
source `0969d9da21b293ac569905bc95bd1fbdcb51f13c` recorded:

- 4,229 CPU tests passed;
- 233 Torch CPU tests passed;
- 824 CUDA tests passed: 412 CuPy and 412 Torch CUDA;
- six native CUDA probes passed;
- 5,288 test items collected, including two optional dual-GPU cases.

Those runs used a single Tesla P100. Collected tests are not necessarily
executed tests, and the optional dual-GPU cases are not a multi-GPU acceptance
claim. The merged baseline
[`5b9d42476f7b921918b7202142f7d39ffd10cdd0`](https://github.com/TheHiddenObserver/statgpu/commit/5b9d42476f7b921918b7202142f7d39ffd10cdd0)
has the identical Git tree `6065449b`; its three hosted workflows and fourteen
checks passed. Neither tree equivalence nor these counts establish that every
feature-specific physical-GPU release check has been rerun. No new general GPU
speedup claim is made.

The detailed changelogs retain earlier feature-specific comparisons and GPU
artifacts with their original sources, validators and hardware. Those records
remain historical when the implementation or validator changes. Before a tag
or PyPI publication, the final release source must pass the checks required by
[RELEASING.md](https://github.com/TheHiddenObserver/statgpu/blob/master/RELEASING.md):
CPU/static/documentation tests, the Python regression matrix, versioned notes,
wheel and sdist validation, clean distribution installs, the
Ubuntu/Windows/macOS wheel smoke matrix, and applicable exact-source physical
CUDA checks. This preparation document does not assert that those final-source
checks have already completed.

## Upgrade notes and known limits

1. **Migrate solver controls by stage.** For behavior-preserving migration of a
   direct penalized estimator, remove deprecated `cpu_solver` and keep the
   existing `solver`. Copying the old `cpu_solver` value into `solver` can
   intentionally change the algorithm. In LassoCV, use `cv_solver` for folds
   and `solver` for the final refit. Explicit coordinate-descent CV remains
   CPU-only. See the
   [migration examples](https://github.com/TheHiddenObserver/statgpu/blob/master/docs/en/guides/penalized-solver-api-migration.md).
2. **Review inference results when upgrading.** Deprecated `cpu_ols` and
   `gpu_ols` strings emit `FutureWarning`; use `post_selection_ols` and choose
   the device independently. The default node-wise penalty now depends on the
   standardized design, with a Kish-style effective sample size for
   nonuniform analytic weights, rather than the response scale. Debiased
   standard errors, intervals and p-values can change even when prediction
   coefficients do not. An explicit positive `nodewise_alpha` selects the
   nuisance penalty, not the model's prediction penalty.
3. **Do not overinterpret conditional inference.** Post-selection OLS and
   SCAD/MCP oracle intervals condition on the selected active set. CV
   inference conditions on the selected penalty and does not correct tuning
   uncertainty. Positive-L2 M-estimation describes a penalized estimating
   equation, not an automatically bias-corrected unpenalized population
   coefficient. Non-Gaussian L1/ElasticNet, group-penalty and penalized-Cox
   coefficient inference remain unsupported. SCAD/MCP oracle inference needs
   a CPU parent fit; an executed GPU fit is rejected rather than transferred.
4. **Expect visible failures in previously unreliable cases.** Oracle
   inference rejects insufficient residual degrees of freedom, unresolved
   convergence, clipped or boundary targets, and certain unrepresentable
   covariance calculations; failure clears fitted state, so refit successfully
   before reusing the model. Only Tweedie and negative-binomial oracle refits
   add relative first-order score checks. Poisson and other families retain
   their existing child-solver stopping criterion, including absolute
   tolerances where used. Small-scale data can require a stricter `tol` or
   rescaling. Range checks do not certify convergence, and relative score
   checks do not bound coefficient or covariance error. RidgeCV rejects
   invalid folds and nonfinite or
   inconsistent moments/results. Its native Gram solves retain conditioning
   and finite-range limits: float64 promotion of already-formed moments
   cannot reconstruct lost factors. Rescale data or disable mixed precision
   when needed. Finite output alone does not certify numerical accuracy.
5. **Respect resampling assumptions.** Gaussian residual bootstrap requires
   unweighted data and nonrobust covariance; weighted, robust/HAC,
   non-Gaussian, Cox and Gaussian L2 variants are not supplied. Standalone
   QuantileRegression uses an i.i.d. residual bootstrap, not a
   heteroscedasticity-robust wild bootstrap. Unequal-size cluster bootstrap
   samples have variable row counts, so custom statistics must accept them.
   Missing cluster labels are invalid; literal string IDs remain valid.
6. **Keep the documented model-specific workarounds.** Ordinary formula
   prediction can still drop missing query rows; scoring now rejects a
   mismatched response rather than broadcasting it. UMAP's documented
   neighborhood/initialization restrictions, KernelPCA failed-refit state,
   KernelPCA/Nystroem Torch placement limitations and knockoff tied-statistic
   problems remain. The tutorial refresh does not repair these algorithms.
   Native float32 L-BFGS can also produce different coefficient trajectories
   across backends; compare objective and stationarity, and use same-backend
   float64 references for tighter reproducibility. Consult the
   [model guides](https://github.com/TheHiddenObserver/statgpu/tree/master/docs/en/models)
   and [float32 numerical guidance](https://github.com/TheHiddenObserver/statgpu/blob/master/docs/en/guides/lbfgs-float32-precision-contract.md).
